high_consensus.description: Valuable and actionable. Mutable per-instance fallback state without declared threading semantics is a real correctness risk under concurrent use. Specifying single-threaded assumption or required locking/thread-local behavior would prevent subtle race bugs.

Critical gap with direct financial impact. 'Enforce on next call' is not a hard cap and can violate operator expectations badly on expensive models. Pre-call estimate behavior and over-cap handling should be explicitly defined.

High-value operability fix. Cache file missing/corrupt/stale is a normal production condition, and unspecified behavior here can cause outages or unpredictable routing. Clear fail-open/fail-closed rules are essential.

blockers.concern: Fallback hysteresis state is per-process and non-persistent, causing inconsistent behavior in multi-process environments
blockers.why_matters: Different processes will disagree on demotion/recovery timing, leading to route flapping, inconsistent latencies, and hard-to-debug incident behavior.
blockers.recommendation: Persist fallback state (shared store/file with lock) or explicitly scope and document single-process guarantees.

blockers.concern: OpenAI response parsing is intentionally fail-loud on unknown output types without degradation path
blockers.why_matters: If OpenAI introduces a new output type, production calls can start failing immediately with UnsupportedResponseShapeError, causing broad outage for routed aliases.
blockers.location: Section 5.4 Response Contract Matrix; Section 6.1 Unsupported response
blockers.recommendation: Introduce a guarded compatibility mode: preserve unknown blocks in metadata, continue with known text/tool content, and alert loudly instead of hard-failing by default.

blockers.concern: Per-session cost cap enforcement is non-atomic and can overspend before blocking
blockers.why_matters: The design checks cap after ledger writes and only raises on the next invocation. A single large call or concurrent calls can exceed budget by a large margin before any stop condition, creating uncontrolled cost exposure.
blockers.location: Section 1.4.4 Cost-Cap Enforcer; Section 5.5 billing semantics
blockers.recommendation: Add pre-flight cost estimation + hard pre-call guardrail, and make cap checks atomic across concurrent writers (file lock or centralized budget state).

blockers.concern: Probe cache trust boundary is undefined; fallback routing can be manipulated via local file tampering
blockers.why_matters: Google fallback decisions read `.run/model-health-cache.json` each request. If that file is stale/corrupt/tampered, traffic can be silently diverted to unintended models, impacting reliability and cost.
blockers.location: Section 1.4.2 Google Adapter; Section 3.5 fallback behavior; Section 1.9 Security Architecture
blockers.recommendation: Define file ownership/permissions, integrity validation (schema + timestamp freshness), and fail-safe behavior when cache is invalid.

blockers.concern: Strict `endpoint_family` validation can create immediate post-upgrade outages for operators with custom OpenAI model blocks
blockers.why_matters: The migration depends on all operator-defined OpenAI entries being updated. Documentation-only mitigation means first run after update can hard fail in production workflows.
blockers.location: Section 3.3 migration policy; Section 3.4 strict validation; Risk R-S1
blockers.recommendation: Provide an automated migrator/linter in update flow and a temporary compatibility grace mode with explicit deadline.
